After the merge commit 0e8b4f7b (2026-09-16T13:58:20Z) it describes. Per T0091, in the order T0108 requires.

merge.gates: All four required gates green on the exact head 529d7489. The governance gate failed once on its first attempt, for a real reason recorded below, and passed after the correction; only that failed job was re-run.
merge.preflight: PASS on all seven default stages.

the_gate_caught_something_preflight_did_.what: PR_METADATA_ZERO_STALE failed: the PR body did not state the recorded status for phase 7 (ACCEPTED_AND_CLOSED) and did not cite D40, the decision that granted it.
the_gate_caught_something_preflight_did_.why_it_is_worth_recording: The PR body is the one authoritative delivery surface that is not committed, so it is the one the Zero-Stale rule cannot check locally against a file. The body was corrected to carry both, and the failed job alone was re-run -- no workflow_dispatch, per the standing rule that a dispatched run reports the same required context and can be inherited as evidence.

behaviour_neutral_by_construction.content: Two test files and one CI script. NO production code changed.
behaviour_neutral_by_construction.why_deploy: So the recorded deployed head keeps describing the binaries -- the standard T0139 established after four binaries were found describing nothing. The rebuild's only effect is the embedded provenance stamp.
behaviour_neutral_by_construction.provenance: APPLIANCE_BUILD = PASS: all six binaries report vcs.revision=0e8b4f7bea1d, modified=false, tags=stayconnect_production, read back out of the artefacts that were written. The appliance carries no Go toolchain, so provenance is carried across by SHA-256: the six staged hashes were compared against the locally verified build before installation, DEPLOYED_SHA and DEPLOYED_BINARIES.txt were rewritten, and the installed set was re-verified in place with sha256sum -c -- all six OK.
behaviour_neutral_by_construction.rollback: /opt/stayconnect/rollback/approved-0e8b4f7b/ holds .prev for all six -- the ec5c7b42 set.

live_state_after.services: All seven active. Two errors in the window, both standing and expected: scd's refusal of SCD_LICENSE_REQUIRED=false on a production build, and pmsd's CONTEXT_CANCELED on its own restart.
live_state_after.checkout_grace: 6 grace entitlements, every one still exactly 3600 seconds, unchanged across the restarts. A deployment that had re-based or extended a historical grace window would show there.
live_state_after.one_new_audit_row_explained: The audit table went 1309 -> 1310 and in-house stays 465 -> 464. That is organic PMS activity, not an effect of the deployment: the new row is a real checkout at 14:03:26Z -- thirty seconds BEFORE the restart -- whose reason_code is NO_ACTIVE_ENTITLEMENT_AT_CHECKOUT, so no grace was granted and the grace count correctly stayed at 6. Quantifying it was the point; an unexplained +1 on a grace audit table is exactly the kind of number that should not be waved past.
live_state_after.pms: The pmsd restart caused its usual reconnect and self-requested resync, which published generation 299 covering 464 records. No operator command, no manual Full Resync.

what_this_delivery_actually_changed: Nothing an operator or guest can observe. It corrected the EVIDENCE for reinstatement -- the transitions are now performed by Processor.ProcessNext rather than by a helper that wrote the expected rows itself -- and it corrected two claims T0146 made: the replay finding there was an artefact of the helper, and replay protection lives at ingestion rather than at resolution. It also closed a gate defect: ./internal/stayengine/ was not in the Phase-5 integration matrix, and the CI log for this delivery now shows it running.

constraints_observed.no_pms_writes: Nothing written to the PMS; no stay or checkout event fabricated. Every rare sequence is a deterministic integration test against a real PostgreSQL.

constraints_observed.guest_state: No guest, stay, entitlement or session row altered on the appliance by this delivery.
